title: VPC onboarding smoke validation suite for Private installs
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define and implement a compact, automatable smoke validation suite run as the final preflight step for Private (VPC) installs. The suite should verify critical surface area quickly (quotas/limits, IAM permissions, DNS resolution, network reachability, GPU capacity and drivers, and Terraform provider compatibility) and return actionable remediation guidance for infra teams.
acceptance_criteria: A runnable Terraform plan + make target that executes the smoke checks in under 10 minutes for a typical VPC footprint
Checks return machine-readable results (exit codes + JSON summary) and human-friendly remediation messages

Coverage includes cloud quotas (compute/GPU/IPs), IAM role/policy sanity, DNS delegation and resolver checks, ephemeral network connectivity checks to Redwood endpoints, and validated GPU instance availability/driver sanity
Integration tests added to CI which simulate a fresh account with synthetic quota limits and validate correct failures/messages
Documentation and runbook committed: Confluence preflight checklist, sample terraform module invocation, and triage playbook for failures
checklist: Quota checks: compute vCPUs, GPU quota per region, elastic IPs, load balancer limits as cloud-provider APIs allow
IAM checks: ability to assume required roles, list/create/attach policies for nodes, KMS encrypt/decrypt permission simulation
DNS checks: verify hosted zone delegation (NS) from customer domain, forward/reverse lookup for control plane endpoints, DNS TTLs and propagation expectations
Network checks: validate route table entries, subnet CIDR overlaps, NAT gateway reachability, required VPC endpoints (S3, STS, ECR), and egress path to Redwood collector endpoints
GPU parity checks: probe for requested instance types in region/AZs, verify GPU driver + CUDA compatibility matrix via an image smoke run
Terraform/IaC sanity: provider version pins, module checksum verification, state locking capability (DynamoDB/remote backend), and plan/apply dry-run smoke
TLS/cert checks: if user provided certs, confirm chain validity and private key access; for managed certs confirm issuance API reachability
Time sync: verify NTP/time offset inside sample instance is within 1s of reference
Container images and registry: CI can pull required images from private registry (ECR/GCR) and authenticate with ephemeral creds
Observability onboarding: verify that Fluentbit/Vector agents can connect to metrics/log ingestion endpoints (port + auth check)
Security posture checks: verify security groups don't allow broad 0.0.0.0/0 SSH or database ports in prod subnets
Upgrade safety checks: verify combination of current runtime version and target upgrade version exist in compatibility matrix before permitting automated upgrade path
technical_plan: Add a new terraform module (redwood.private.preflight) that exposes a make target: make preflight-smoke --region=<r> --acct=<id>

Implement a lightweight runner (go binary) that queries cloud quotas, performs IAM assume-role flow, runs DNS lookups, and launches a micro 'smoke' instance with a test image to validate GPU drivers and networking
Smoke runner will emit a JSON summary (checks: pass/warn/fail, raw evidence logs, remediation string, docs link) and will exit with code 0 if all critical checks pass, non-zero otherwise
Use existing provider clients from infra/lib to keep auth consistent; include retry/backoff and rate-limit handling
Wrap quota checks with a heuristics layer: treat near-limit (<20% headroom) as warn and provide suggested reduction/limit request templates
Add CI harness that spins up an ephemeral sandbox account using org test credentials and toggles synthetic quota caps to validate failure modes
Store canonical remediation snippets in Confluence and reference them by slug in the JSON output to keep runner lightweight
rollout_notes: Phase 1: internal alpha run on two accounts (us-west-2, eu-central-1) with infra oncall following checklist
Phase 2: incorporate runner into onboarding playbook and exposed as part of the private-deploy terraform template in customer onboarding repo
Phase 3: expose as a CLI plugin for Solutions Engineers and integrate into the provisioning pipeline (post-apply verification)
Pin initial rollout to runtime-1.25 release so upgrade-check matrix is stable
